scope: Private offline research only; one trusted local SQLite file.
independent_checks: Independent reader sees zero rows between a committed withdrawal and resumed publication and zero immediately afterward.
A fresh post-withdrawal snapshot sees no current result. An already-open WAL reader may retain its old snapshot; opening a fresh read must give the new status.
When the final writer already holds the SQLite write lock, an attempted withdrawal from a distinct connection cannot commit until the result transaction releases it.
A conflict on the same advisory prevents current publication even if Scout retains the preceding current_state pointer. Another advisory's unrelated event must not invalidate this result.
Repeated consumption on two connections and reopening the database preserve result identity, historical payload, version/digest/source attribution and no extra current row.
A normalized product and an explicit selected alias must both be supported by the same immutable raw source; independently inspect the fixture rather than comparing output to itself.
